cells.requirement: All 1 to 4 unit properties are exempt from Jersey City's rent control regulations.
Landlords in Jersey City Code § 218-12 are prohibited from using algorithmic rent coordination services.

The Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act makes it unlawful for a rental property owner or coordinator to use algorithmic software that collects competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels.

Housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about an applicant's criminal record prior to issuing a conditional offer of rental housing, and are prohibited from discriminating in housing based on protected classes including race, religion, color, national origin, sex, disability, and source of lawful income.
Landlords and their agents cannot charge a residential rental application or screening fee exceeding $50, subject to annual adjustments based on the Consumer Price Index.

Landlords are prohibited from charging a security deposit exceeding one and one-half times one month's rent, and must deposit funds in an interest-bearing account, returning the deposit plus interest within 30 days of lease termination.
Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction.
No landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% under the city rent leveling ordinance.

Landlords renting residential units in Hoboken are prohibited from using software, algorithms, or data-sharing platforms to coordinate, recommend, or implement rental prices, lease terms, or occupancy levels among competing landlords.
Landlords may increase rent annually based on the applicable monthly Consumer Price Index-Urban (CPI-U) percentage published for the relevant month, provided they give proper written notice.
In properties subject to rent control, landlords cannot increase rent by more than the applicable percentage posted or 4%, whichever is lower.

Landlords may not remove residential tenants or fail to renew leases except for specific statutory grounds of good cause. Displaced tenants due to illegal occupancy are entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent if the municipality has no ordinance.
